title: Shikimic acid ameliorates immobilization-induced muscle atrophy through regulation of inflammation and muscle protein homeostasis.
authors: Kim, Mi-Bo; Yoo, Jihee; Moon, Chae Young; Hwang, Jae-Kwan; Kang, Hyunju
one_liner_zh: 该文研究莽草酸通过NF-kB和PI3K/Akt/mTOR通路改善固定诱导的肌肉萎缩，仅含分子对接分析，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Immobilization induces skeletal muscle atrophy by disrupting muscle protein homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of muscle mass and function. Shikimic acid (SA), a plant-derived organic acid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, has not been previously evaluated in immobilization-associated muscle atrophy. This study aimed to determine whether SA attenuates skeletal muscle atrophy by regulating inflammation and muscle protein turnover using cellular and animal models. In tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFalpha)-induced L6 myotubes, SA significantly suppressed inflammatory cytokine expression through inhibition of nuclear factor-kappaB) (NF-kappaB) signaling and attenuated forkhead box O3a (FoxO3a)-dependent protein degradation, while restoring protein kinase B (Akt)/mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR)-dependent anabolic signaling to promote myogenic differentiation and protein synthesis. In an immobilization-induced muscle atrophy model in mice, SA administration prevented declines in grip strength and exercise capacity and preserved skeletal muscle mass and myofiber cross-sectional area. At the molecular level, SA alleviated inflammatory responses and restored the balance between protein synthesis and degradation in the tibialis anterior muscle. Furthermore, molecular docking analysis revealed that SA interacts with the activation pocket of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), providing structural insight into the mechanism of anabolic signaling reactivation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SA mitigates immobilization-induced skeletal muscle atrophy by suppressing NF-kappaB-mediated inflammatory signaling and restoring muscle protein turnover through reactivation of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway, highlighting its potential as a functional compound for preventing disuse-induced muscle loss.
abstract_zh: 固定术通过破坏肌肉蛋白质稳态诱导骨骼肌萎缩，导致肌肉质量和功能进行性丧失。莽草酸（shikimic acid, SA）是一种具有抗炎和抗氧化特性的植物来源有机酸，此前尚未在固定术相关肌肉萎缩中评估其作用。本研究旨在利用细胞和动物模型，确定SA是否通过调节炎症和肌肉蛋白质周转来减轻骨骼肌萎缩。在肿瘤坏死因子α（tumor necrosis factor alpha, TNFα）诱导的L6肌管中，SA通过抑制核因子-κB（nuclear factor-kappaB, NF-κB）信号显著抑制炎症细胞因子表达，并减弱叉头框蛋白O3a（forkhead box O3a, FoxO3a）依赖性蛋白质降解，同时恢复蛋白激酶B（protein kinase B, Akt）/哺乳动物雷帕霉素靶蛋白（mechanistic target of rapamycin, mTOR）依赖性合成代谢信号，以促进肌源性分化和蛋白质合成。在小鼠固定术诱导的肌肉萎缩模型中，SA给药防止了握力和运动能力下降，并保留了骨骼肌质量和肌纤维横截面积。在分子水平上，SA缓解了胫骨前肌中的炎症反应，并恢复了蛋白质合成与降解之间的平衡。此外，分子对接分析显示，SA与磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（phosphoinositide 3-kinase, PI3K）的激活口袋相互作用，为合成代谢信号重激活机制提供了结构见解。综上所述，这些发现表明，SA通过抑制NF-κB介导的炎症信号并重激活PI3K/Akt/mTOR信号通路恢复肌肉蛋白质周转，从而减轻固定术诱导的骨骼肌萎缩，凸显其作为预防废用性肌肉丢失的功能性化合物的潜力。
